Implemented the approved seven-step plan under the recorded maintainer completion rule. Developer-owned focused checks pass. The approved inputs, REVIEW.md, VALIDATION.md, protected files, cleanup authorization and the existing detached-session regression were not changed. ## Implementation and producer audit

1. Added coordinator-only context scopes to storageuse. They own durable uses, canonical repository identity, forbidden original source paths and pinned temporary-directory parents. ControlRoot resolves the normal OS user-cache location plus `swarm-use`, outside cache grants. ResourceFor shares the existing `cache:`/`scratch:` identity format. No record format, worker protocol, flag or configuration field changed. Finish uses an independent five-second context; panic, failed/uncertain stop, cleanup identity failure and failed completion writes preserve pending evidence. Normal host completion accepts exit plus successful StopVerified; Bubblewrap keeps its existing stronger namespace boundary.
2. Build/dependency producers admit before directory creation, migration, marker reads, prefetch and cache access. Legacy migration admits source and destination and preserves unknown target coverage. Invalid persistent layouts retain the existing separately admitted scratch fallback; durable admission errors cannot silently select it. Nested fallback caches share their admitted outer scratch root. Scratch cache creation rejects substituted symlink components through safefs. Go, Rust, Python and Node prefetch allocate admitted scratch, preserve verified-stop status separately from fetch outcome, and finish only after remaining copies/marker work and the enclosing consumers.
3. Native and delegated runtime scopes retain scratch/caches through callbacks, session observation, timeout recovery and import. Native command failure/cancellation with a verified stop can complete; failed stops retain evidence. OMP and OpenCode needed the same minimal verified-stop plumbing. Reviewer snapshots have an outer scope through artifact import. ToolExecutor only reacquires from an inherited coordinator scope: a separate internal-tools process never creates coordinator evidence from its cache arguments or environment. Its complete lifetime is already owned by the enclosing delegated run. No mounts, sandbox policy, credential forwarding or process-group strategy changed.
4. ExecuteWork owns preflight and all later roles, including errors before claims. Checkpoint planning and independent/upstream review calls establish their own scope when necessary. The checkpoint and upstream review snapshots are admitted before creation. Standalone dependency preparation completes its own preparation invocation; subsequent independent runtime readers reacquire before access. Dependencies remains worker-visible data only. There is no new claim authority in storage registration.
5. Validation owns cache preparation, warm-up/marker hits, all checks, retries, diagnostic base/checkpoint reruns and checkout teardown. Standalone check/warm-up invocations establish an owner. Host checks propagate verified-stop failures independently of command errors and retain original exit-code reporting. Checkout cleanup preserves retained runs and uses pinned temporary-root removal before pruning stale Git worktree registrations. Diagnostic cleanup errors are reported in the repair summary.
6. Inventory observes the same canonical cache keys while retaining repository display names, and indexes only validated managed scratch layouts (including sibling Rust prefetch scratch and workflow snapshot prefixes). Indexed records precede prefix-only discovery so durable evidence is not discarded as a duplicate. Orphan, legacy and mismatched identities remain unknown. CLI report supplies the shared trusted control root without creating it. No cleanup eligibility path, deletion command, flag or help contract was added.
